Direct Gateway URL for a local process or Kubernetes port-forward. Gateway health and readiness requests use this variable.
Captured automatically by the automated verification folder; never commit a populated session token.
Application admin username, NOT PostgreSQL emerald. The automated Kubernetes runner reads it from emerald-security-credentials. Fill privately only for the Postman UI.
Application admin password, NOT the PostgreSQL password. The automated runner reads it from Kubernetes in memory. Never commit a populated credential.
Option B uses the Gateway HTTP port-forward at localhost:8080. HTTPS edge scenarios are opt-in manual requests.

NGINX Gateway Fabric HTTPS entry for Kubernetes. The documented local HTTPS port-forward maps 8443 to the generated NGINX data-plane Service port 443. Trust the local certificate; do not disable verification by default.
Manual HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect demonstration only. Never send login credentials over this URL. Port-forward local 8080 to the generated NGINX data-plane Service port 80.
Use a new safe key for each test run. Reuse it with the same payload to verify replay; reuse it with a changed payload only for the conflict request. Records expire after 24 hours.
Change to an unused active-member mobile number before first creation.
Keep false for collection-runner verification. Enable only when deliberately running selected manual reference requests.
